title: A Bad Move with the Wrong Name
body: There is a notoriously weak chess opening called the Damiano Defense. Strangely, an early chess writer named Damiano actually wrote a book warning people never to play this move because it was so bad. Instead of getting credit for his helpful advice, history played a trick on him by naming the terrible move after him anyway.

variants.lucy: Long ago in the sixteenth century, a thoughtful writer named Damiano crafted a book to protect chess players from making a terrible mistake at the very start of the game. He carefully explained why this particular opening move would leave your pieces weak and unprotected. Yet, in a quiet twist of history, people began calling that exact, clumsy setup by his own name instead.
variants.luca: Imagine writing a brilliant guidebook to warn players away from a disastrous opening trap, only for the world to name the trap after you! That is the wild trick history played on a writer named Damiano back in the fifteen-hundreds. He loudly declared that this specific start was a terrible mistake, but today, players still call this awful defense by his name.

source.book: The Art of the Game of Chess
source.author: Ruy López, trans. Andrew Soltis & Michael J. McGrath
